g.text: Docker Desktop as a Swarm node: what is documented, what is a hypothesis
Not tested. The point of this diagram is to keep facts and guesses visibly apart.
other swarm node
(manager or worker)
Windows host
Docker Desktop VM (private NAT address)
Engine listens: 2377 7946 4789
swarm node would live here
connect to 2377
forwarded to the Engine? (hypothesis: no rule by default)
Documented (green):
The VM has a private NAT address (typically 192.168.65.3); per-container IPs are not reachable from the host.
Inbound traffic reaches the VM through a host-side process that forwards PUBLISHED container ports.
Docker Desktop's docs assume a Swarm can be active on it (changing its internal IP ranges requires leaving any active Swarm).
Hypotheses (red, UNTESTED):
H1 Nothing forwards 2377 / 7946 / 4789 to the Engine in the default setup, so other nodes cannot reach it.
H2 The user-space proxy re-originates flows, which could change the outer source IP of VXLAN packets and confuse the VTEP.
H3 WSL mirrored networking (or netsh portproxy to the WSL VM) might make it work; MTU and firewall rules would still need care.
Experiment to settle it: Docker Desktop + WSL2 mirrored mode, `docker swarm init --advertise-addr <host LAN IP>`, join from a Linux box, then test 2377/7946/4789, then
an overlay ping. Record Docker Desktop and WSL versions with the result.
